title.orig: The brain is wider than the sky
title.en: The brain is wider than the sky

edition.en: Poems, Third Series (1896), edited by Mabel Loomis Todd, on Project Gutenberg (eBook 12242)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 12242 所录《诗集·第三辑》（1896），托德编

basis.en: First published in 1896 in Poems, Third Series, after the author’s death in 1886; the editor, Mabel Loomis Todd, died in 1932.
basis.zh: 1896 年首次出版于《诗集·第三辑》，作者已于 1886 年去世；编者梅布尔·卢米斯·托德卒于 1932 年。

note.en: Titled “The Brain” by its editor. Three stanzas of measurement, the mind against the sky, the sea and God, each tested with a homely image: side by side, blue to blue, pound for pound. The last line, “as syllable from sound”, is the kind of distinction only a poet who worked in syllables would think to make.
note.zh: 编者题为“大脑”。三节诗都是测量：拿心智去比天空、大海和上帝，每一次都用家常的意象来试——并排放、蓝对蓝、一磅对一磅。最后一行“如音节之于声音”，是只有以音节为业的诗人才会想到的区分。

excerpt.orig:
The brain is wider than the sky,
For, put them side by side,
The one the other will include
With ease, and you beside.
excerpt.en:
The brain is wider than the sky,
For, put them side by side,
The one the other will include
With ease, and you beside.
excerpt.zh:
大脑比天空更宽广，
因为，把它们并排放着，
一个就能把另一个装下，
还轻轻松松装下你。
